choices: a stone whose colour changes with the direction of observation
a stone that glows under UV
a stone that changes colour with heat
questions.why: Light is absorbed differently depending on the axis.

questions.q: How is the London dichroscope made?
choices: A glass prism and a slit
Two polarizing filters glued at right angles in a folding loupe
A calcite crystal in a tube
questions.why: Each half of the lens lets through one direction of vibration.

questions.q: What does a red spinel show in the dichroscope?
choices: No change: the two windows are the same
questions.why: It is isotropic: it is not a ruby.

questions.q: How many colours can a biaxial stone show?
What is an advantage of the dichroscope?
choices: It works even on a set stone, without touching it
questions.why: Neither of the two models touches the stone.

questions.q: Why does a garnet show the same colour in the two windows A and B?
choices: It is isotropic: there is no pleochroism
questions.why: Cubic stones have only one colour.

questions.q: What is needed for the dichroscope to give a result?
questions.why: A very pale or colourless stone gives little result.

questions.q: Which model uses a crystal of Iceland spar?
questions.why: It gives two images side by side.
